head: 5e2bc38de8abbbf31796435db8f062f345637e5f
decided_by: A1 per frozen acceptance criteria (architecture_freeze.json pandera_acceptance_criteria)

criteria.criterion: identical accepted/rejected row sets and reason attribution vs native frozen schema
criteria.evidence: on RAW boundary fixtures (10-60 rows): one type-poisoned raw row (e.g. float timestamp) makes the strict dtype contract reject the WHOLE batch where the native validator rejects just that row — crypto trades, forex bid/ask, stocks quotes; macro series row sets agree but attribution differs (native MALFORMED_SHAPE vs schema-selection UNKNOWN_EVENT_TYPE)
criteria.supplementary: on pre-normalized canonical batches pandera matches native exactly (same rows, same attribution) — the boundary it can serve is post-normalization, which is not the provider boundary the spike scoped

criteria.criterion: deterministic errors independent of row order
no mutation of the input DataFrame

criteria.evidence: median pandera/native ratio 81-267x on small fixtures; 8.3x on a 2000-row trade batch (native ~0.040s vs pandera ~0.331s)

criteria.criterion: optional import isolation (hot path independent of pandas/pandera)

conclusion: native frozen schema validator RETAINED; pandera 0.33.1 remains installed as a dev-only dependency of record for the spike evidence; it is not imported by any production module (deferred_import_scan verifies)
